The auction is for NORTH_CAROLINA_AVENUE. The current bid is $59 and the minimum raise is $60. I will bid $60 to win the property. I can mortgage it for $150. This blocks p4 from completing a green set.

p1 cannot complete a green monopoly without Pacific. p4's mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue generates no rent. I have four houses on each pink property but no houses remaining to build hotels.

p4 has $763 cash and owns Reading and B&O railroads, light blues with four houses each, and mortgaged utilities. They are in jail.

Bidding $60 nets a $90 profit after mortgaging the property. I will keep the $150 cap because buying at or below that price is cash-positive.

Standard Monopoly rent for Park Place with three houses is $1100 and Boardwalk with four houses is $1700. Selling all twelve pink houses would raise $600, giving total liquidity of $1326. This covers both properties.

Mortgaging the pink properties would not cover the full $1700 Boardwalk rent. St. Charles, States, and Virginia mortgages total only about $220. The shortfall is roughly $374.

The shortfall to Boardwalk is $154. I will not drop out of the auction. p4 is matching every dollar bid and has enough cash to keep raising.

No houses remain in the bank, so completing a green monopoly would require players to sell existing houses. This reduces the urgency of blocking p4 from acquiring North Carolina Avenue. Even without a full set, the property still generates rent.

- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid or drop out on the current auction.

The current bid is $63. I will raise to $64. I plan to mortgage North Carolina Avenue for $150. This keeps my cash near the $1100 cap and blocks player 4 from completing a PA+NC pair.

Winning at $64 nets $86 after mortgaging. Player 4 cannot complete a green monopoly without Pacific, so they may be bidding to block me or acquire another piece. I have a strong pink monopoly with four houses each on St. Charles, States, and Virginia.

Player 1 has dangerous dark blues but only $29 cash. Player 4 owns fully built light blues and is in jail. Pacific is mortgaged, so neither player can complete a green monopoly alone.

Player 1 also owns a yellow monopoly with one house on each property. I will keep raising the bid to $64 rather than jumping, so player 4 pays more and bleeds cash.

If player 4 bids up to $149, they would only profit minimally after mortgaging. I should not drop out because that would let them acquire the property cheaply and potentially trade with player 1 for Pacific to complete a green monopoly. I have no greens to block, so winning North Carolina Avenue is the better option.

I am weighing a bid above $150 to deny player 4 the PA+NC pair. Park Place with three houses costs $1100 in rent, so preserving cash for dark blue rent coverage is a key constraint.
